citations.section: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Policy Wording) > 3. Pre-Authorisation > 3.3 Contents of a Pre-Authorisation Request
citations.quote:
### 3.3 Contents of a Pre-Authorisation Request
The request must state the diagnosis with ICD/SNOMED code, the proposed line of treatment, the estimated cost, the expected length of stay, and the treating doctor's justification of medical necessity, along with supporting investigation reports.

citations.section: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Policy Wording) > 3. Pre-Authorisation > 3.2 Emergency Admissions
citations.quote:
### 3.2 Emergency Admissions
For an emergency admission, the pre-authorisation request must be submitted within 24 hours of admission. Emergency treatment shall not be denied solely because authorisation was sought after admission within this period.

citations.section: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Policy Wording) > 3. Pre-Authorisation > 3.1 When Pre-Authorisation Is Required
citations.quote:
## 3. Pre-Authorisation  
### 3.1 When Pre-Authorisation Is Required
Prior authorisation from the Company or its TPA is mandatory for (a) every planned In-patient Hospitalisation, and (b) any treatment where the estimated cost exceeds ₹25,000.

citations.section: Community-acquired Pneumonia — Admission Criteria > Medical Necessity of Admission
citations.quote:
## Medical Necessity of Admission
Admission is justified by hypoxaemia (SpO₂ < 92%), haemodynamic instability, inability to take oral medication, or a high severity score. A chest X-ray confirming consolidation is required.

citations.section: Community-acquired Pneumonia — Admission Criteria > Red Flags in Billing
citations.quote:
## Red Flags in Billing
Repeated short admissions for pneumonia in young patients without hypoxaemia or radiological confirmation are not consistent with guidelines.
